notable_absence.finding: No RBAC role or privilege is named anywhere on this page for --create/--edit/--delete/--list, despite Analytics link management being exactly the kind of Full-Admin-gated area the promoted registry documents elsewhere for sibling REST endpoints (analytics:library-upload and both restart APIs are stated as Full Admin only). The CLI reference never states which of the 56 Server roles, or which privilege, is required to run any of its actions - consistent with the round's lighter-TW-review hypothesis for engineer-authored CLI pages.

cross_component_finding: Two internal inconsistencies suggest this page gets less TW scrutiny than the REST reference for the same feature. First, the EXAMPLES section's delete command reads '$ couchbase-cli analytics-link-setup ... --delete --scope Default --link east' - using a bare '--link' flag that is never defined anywhere in OPTIONS (only '--name <name>' is documented as the delete/edit target). Second, --dataverse is kept as a working deprecated alias for --scope with no removal version ever given. Both are the kind of drift-with-no-catch a TW review pass over a REST reference typically removes; here they persist. Separately, the HOST FORMATS, CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION and 'Part of the couchbase-cli suite' boilerplate blocks are reproduced byte-for-byte identically across every one of this batch's 7 pages, confirming they come from a shared doc-generation template rather than per-page authorship - the divergence in this round is entirely in the substantive OPTIONS/EXAMPLES content, never in the boilerplate.
cross_product_finding: analytics-link-setup and enterprise-analytics-link-setup are NOT a copy-paste-with-rename pair: this page exposes ~30 discrete flags across five link-type-specific option groups (Couchbase/S3/Azure Blob/Azure Data Lake/GCS), while its Enterprise Analytics sibling collapses all of that into two generic flags (--link-details <json> / --link-details-path <path>). The interface was redesigned around a JSON payload, not renamed. Given that redesign, this page (and its --dataverse/--scope pairing, matching analytics:analytics-scope's own documented dataverse-to-scope rename) reads as the CURRENT, actively-maintained surface, while the EA sibling looks like an early, deliberately minimal placeholder for a still-developing product line - see that record's own findings for the specific evidence.
